title: Jump Festa 2027 Confirms Packed Schedule With Major Anime & Manga Reveals Teased
content:
Shueisha’s next Jump Festa event is fast approaching, and now the publisher has confirmed the full schedule for the event with a tease of some of the major franchises that will have something on offer later this year. Jump Festa is the annual convention taking place in Japan each December where Shueisha shows off all of the projects that they have in the works. This year is no different as there are many franchises with new anime and manga releases to update fans on.

Taking place over the December 19-20 weekend in Japan, the official schedule for Jump Festa 2027 has been reveale d. These include “Jump Super Stage” which are some of the most high profile Shonen Jump franchises, and Jump Studio, which are some of the lesser known titles that still have something to share. The official website for Jump Festa 2027 has now confirmed the official schedule of events (in JST) and it breaks down as such:

Jump Festa 2027 Confirms Schedule of Events

Jump Super Stage

Saturday, December 19th (in JST)

• 11:40-12:10 – Kagurabachi

• 12:25-12:55 – Oblivion Battery

• 13:10-13:40 – The Prince of Tennis II

• 13:55-14:25 – World Trigger

• 14:40-15:10 – Sakamoto Days

• 15:25-15:55 – Jujutsu Kaisen

• 16:10-16:40 – My Hero Academia

• 16:55-17:25 – Naruto

Sunday, December 20th

• 11:40-12:10 – Haikyu!!

• 12:25-12:55 – Chainsaw Man

• 13:10-13:40 – DAN DA DAN

• 13:55-14:25 – SPY x FAMILY

• 14:40-15:10 – Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba

• 15:25-15:55 – Akane-banashi

• 16:45-17:35 – One Piece

Jump Studio

Saturday, December 19th (in JST)

• 11:40-12:10 – Phantom Busters

• 12:50-13:20 – Girl meets Rock!

• 14:00-14:30 – Kaiju No. 8

• 15:10-15:40 – Nue’s Exorcist

• 16:20-16:50 – Kindergarten WARS

Sunday, December 20th

• 11:40-12:10 – Katekyo Hitman REBORN!

• 12:50-13:20 – Mashle: Magic and Muscles

• 14:00-14:30 – Witch Watch

• 15:10-15:40 – Bleach

• 16:20-16:50 – Dark Gathering

Jump Station

• Black Clover

• Kochikame

• High School Family: Kokosei Kazoku

• Mission: Yozakura Family

• Chained Soldier

• Marriagetoxin

• Mr. Cliche

• The Bugle Call

• Gokurakugai

What’s Going Down at Jump Festa 2027?

The schedule for the Jump Station events has yet to be confirmed at this time, but each of the confirmed events thus far are for some major titles that fans need to keep an eye out for. These events are also teasing that members of an anime’s voice cast will be in attendance for each presentation, and that makes it all the more excited as to what could be potentially revealed . For anime, it’s usually an update revealing the first looks at some of what’s coming our way next.

Some of these events make their way online, but a lot of the time they are relegated to those who are able to attend the event in person in Japan. Major franchises like One Piece, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba, Jujutsu Kaisen and more all have new anime releases in the works for the immediate future, so this event is likely going to be a big one with some key updates for what’s to come. There are potentially even more surprises than what has been previously teased thus far too.

With Jump Festa 2027 around the corner, what are you hoping to see revealed during the event? What kinds of Shonen Jump anime updates are you hoping to get for the next year and beyond? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: My Hero Academia Spinoff Gets New Streaming Home With Major Update
content:
Written and illustrated by Kohei Horikoshi, My Hero Academia remains one of the most successful anime and manga franchises of all time. While the main story is long over, fans always have something new to look forward to. One of the most anticipated updates is the third season of the spin-off series, My Hero Academia: Vigilante s . The anime is based on a manga of the same name written by Hideyuki and illustrated by Court Betten. It serves as the official prequel spin-off to the main story, centering around new characters. The story takes place five years before Izuku Midoriya acquired his quirk and enrolled in U.A. High.

The spin-off has released two seasons so far, and while fans await updates on Season 3, Netflix finally began streaming the series . Both seasons of the anime landed on the platform on October 16th, 2026 across regions in the U.S., UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. While the main story’s seasons, movies, and the spin-off were already available in a few regions of Asia, Netflix is expanding the audience by bringing it into the West. Vigilantes is the latest MHA addition to the platform. However, the anime is currently available in Japanese audio with English subtitles on Netflix, while Crunchyroll has long been streaming the dubbed episodes.

Is My Hero Academia: Vigilantes Considered a Canon Story?

Although it’s a spin-off written by someone other than Horikoshi, Vigilantes is still considered canon. Horikoshi actively supervised the spin-off, reviewed its storyboards, and provided input on the plotlines. Not only that, but Koichi Haimawari, the protagonist of the spin-off, also made an appearance in the final stretch of the main story. His cameo basically confirmed that he exists within the same world as Deku and the others. The spin-off also includes major characters from the main story, including Aizawa, Midnight, All For One, and more. Apart from introducing original characters, the spin-off also gave more depth to Aizawa with his new backstory . All For One continues to scheme from within the shadows before the brutal fight against All Might, where both sides sustained long-lasting effects.

My Hero Academia: Vigilantes Delays Season 3 Announcement Despite Its Popularity

While the spin-off isn’t nearly as big a hit as the main story, it still has enough popularity to get a third season. However, even though the second season ended in March this year, there haven’t been any updates regarding Season 3 . The animation studio has stayed silent on the anime’s future even though more than half of the manga hasn’t been adapted yet. However, there’s still a possibility that Studio Bones will return with this fan-favorite series before long.

The second season finale ended after a two-year time skip, with Koichi referencing his life as the Crawler is nearing its end, confirming that the story will take a major turn in Season 3. With the animation studio being occupied by multiple projects, including the new anime short My Hero Academia: I Am a Hero Too , the delay isn’t that shocking. The anime still needs two more seasons to wrap up the story, and we might get an update during this year’s Jump Festa if we’re lucky. Since My Hero Academia is already taking the stage during the convention , there is a possibility that Vigilantes will shed light on its future as well.

Are you going to watch My Hero Academia: Vigilantes now that it’s streaming with Netflix? Let us know in the comments!

title: Actor Michael Forest Dies at 97
content:
Forest had numerous roles in live-action television series and anime. His television roles include Apollo in Star Trek , Father Joe Coogan in The Dick Van Dyke Show , Anastacio in Zorro , Steve in the "Black Leather Jackets" episode of The Twilight Zone , and Olympius in Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue . He also played characters in Bonanza , Gilligan's Island , Rawhide , Get Smart , and the film Cast Away .

His anime roles include Kubota in Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex , Alex Rosewater in The Big O , Kojima in Mobile Suit Gundam: The 08th MS Team , Braya in Eureka Seven , Takeshi Kusumi in Patlabor WXIII , and Dr. Seijiro Inui in Paprika .

title: 19 Years Later, Cancelled Shonen Jump Series Returns With English Dub for Anime Revival
content:
A major Shonen Jump series has kicked off its official anime revival 19 years after it was originally cancelled, and Crunchyroll has now starting to release the official English dub for the new anime series. It’s been a wild year for Shonen Jump as fans have started to see many cancelled projects returning with their own official anime adaptations . Some of these cancellations have made fans wait for much longer before their anime debuts, and that’s the case for Toshiaki Iwashiro’s Psyren . It’s taken nearly 20 years for its anime to hit.

Psyren first made its debut with Shonen Jump in 2007, and ran for 100 chapters before it was cancelled with the magazine in 2010. 16 years after that cancellation, the franchise has now returned with its own official TV anime adaptation now airing new episodes as part of the Fall 2026 anime schedule. And luckily for fans of English dubbed anime, the first episode of the dub release is now available for streaming with Crunchyroll as part of their packed slate.

Psyren English Dub Confirms Crunchyroll Release Date & Voice Cast

The first episode of Psyren’ s official English dub release is now streaming with Crunchyroll as of Monday, October 19th, and new episodes will then be launching on a weekly basis. This is only two episodes behind the Japanese language release of the series , so dub fans won’t have to wait too long to catch up with everything that’s happened so far. Directed by Dani Chambers for Crunchyroll, the voice cast for the English dub has been confirmed with the debut of its first episode as well.

The English dub cast for Psyren currently includes Dylan Ray Owen as Ageha, Kelly Greenshield as Amamiya, Katelyn Barr as Fubuki, Kevin D. Thelwell as Hiroki, Jacob Browning as Miyake, Abigail Blythe as Nemesis Q, Derrick Snow as Okumura, Mauricio Ortiz-Segura as Saka, and Daniel Van Thomas as Usui. Any potential new cast additions will be revealed as their characters make their respective debuts through the course of the rest of the anime’s debut season this Fall. But a proper episode count has yet to be confirmed as of this time.

What to Know for Psyren

The production staff bringing Psyren to screens after all this time include Katsumi Ono serving as director with animation production handled by Satelight. Shin Yoshida is handling its scripts, Akira Okuma is designing the characters, and Takashi Ohmama, Tatsuhiko Saiki, Shu Kanematsu are composing the music. Toshiaki Iwashiro has been working closely with the production team for the adaptation, and it’s been touted as a complete take on the original manga release.

If this proves to be a success, then it means other cancelled Shonen Jump franchises can get their chance with an anime revival in the future. This is the third revival anime of a cancelled series we’ve seen this year following Black Torch this Summer , and Super Psychic Policeman Chojo also airing its new episodes this Fall. If any of these shows are popular enough to warrant a continuation with original anime stories in the future, then we’re in totally uncharted territory for Shonen Jump from then on.

Are you going to be catching up with Psyren now that it’s released an English dub? What English dubs are you most excited to check out this Fall? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: One Piece’s Luffy Became a Real Captain With This Major Turning Point (& It’s a Fan-Favorite Arc)
content:
Monkey D. Luffy started off as a pure-hearted youngster that yearned to become King of Pirates when One Piece kicked off 30 years ago . He quickly gained the audience’s adulation, taking down villains and scrounging together an unlikely crew. However, he became a real captain and a true friend when he defended Nami and took down the Fish-Men at Arlong Park.

Luffy showed care for his crew from the very beginning , and never relented. He set Zoro free from Marine captivity, assisted Usopp in protecting Syrup Village and stopped Don Krieg’s Pirates from destroying the Baratie, where Sanji grew up and honed his skills as a chef. All of those different situations ended with collective, undying trust in the Straw-Hat’s Captain. But it really started to all come together for Luffy as as a captain when it came to saving Nami from Arlong.

Luffy Not Only Saves Nami, He Frees Her

The difference with Nami from the other crew members was that she betrayed him at first. All the others jumped right into his crew and never looked back, but Nami always carried a shady part of her story from her introduction. She was shown stealing numerous times and not coming across completely honest. Luffy could’ve turned his back on her and tried to find another navigator. But without hesitation he chased after her, and put his faith in that fact she wouldn’t turn on him without good reason.

During the Baratie arc she stole the Going Merry, including the treasure they had accumulated so far, and headed back to Arlong Park. There she hoped to finally purchase her village back for the price of $100,000,000 Berries. Instead, the sadistic captain Arlong betrayed her and stole all the money to keep her indebted to him. Destitute and heartbroken, Nami then tried to violently remove her Arlong tattoo by using a knife and tearfully stabbed her shoulder over and over again. After realizing she couldn’t do this alone anymore, she asked Luffy for help .

Then as Luffy watched Nami break down, he put his iconic straw hat on her head says, “Of course, that’s what friends do.” Marching down to Arlong Park to use his justified anger to not only beat Arlong, but make him pay, the climax of this fight really gave fans a better look into Luffy as a character. When Arlong showed him all the maps Nami charted over the years, it disgust Luffy to find out the captain had used her for his own gain. Luffy would never manipulate her in that way, and then ends the fight for good with a Gum-Gum Battle Axe to split Arlong Park down the middle.

The Show’s Tone Makes A 180-Degree Turn With Nami’s Story

It’s a moment that’s deeply satisfying in the anime and live-action , but also hammers home the point that this isn’t a stereotypical pirate story. Series creator Eiichiro Oda leaves little crumbs all across the first few sagas about what kind of a person Luffy is. Still, it’s the overt passion in this arc that solidifies the characterization of the caring, rubber captain. Luffy wants to be King of the Pirates, but he won’t sacrifice his moral code to accomplish his goals. He wants everyone else to succeed around him too, specifically his friends.

The whole arc clicks up the series a few notches of seriousness too. There were steps where it looked like the show had a lighter, comedic side for the bulk of its preceding episodes. Alvida, Helmeppo and Buggy’s storylines were all made to be mostly comic relief. The themes started to shift with Usopp’s introduction as while Usopp was a goofy character in his own right, his motivations were not. He wanted to save Kaya, save his town, and defeat Captain Kuro and the Black Cat Pirates. That arc started to shift more of the tone on its head that Arlong Park puts a definitive stake in later.

Arlong Park brought up darker themes like Nami’s adoptive mother Bell-Mere being murdered (which orphaned her and her sister), and dove deep into Nami’s enslavement to Arlong. This arc defines what the core of One Piece and Luffy are all about . It’s a story about a ragtag group of deeply loyal friends that prove they can conquer anything with the help of each other. Although that may sound a little cheesy on the outside, it’s what plenty of the best anime embody. What do you think? Is Arlong Park where One Piece takes its dramatic turn with Luffy as Captain? Let us know in the comments.

title: The Simpsons’ New Apu Breaks Silence on Taking Over Role (& Explains Casting Process)
content:
The Simpsons has officially reintroduced Apu back into the animated series with Season 38’s newest episode, and the new voice star behind the role has opened up about joining the long running series and explaining how the secretive casting process for the character worked out. The Simpsons had a lot of surprises in store for fans this past weekend as not only did it shock with a second Treehouse of Horror special for the season , but then revealed that Apu is now back in the official timeline after missing for nearly a decade.

Formerly voiced by Hank Azaria before his retiring from the character officially in 2020, Apu has been relegated to background cameos and gags since his last speaking appearance in 2017. But The Simpsons Season 38 has now brought him back with new voice actor Sunil Maholtra , and the new star opened up to Variety about joining the long running series with such a divisive role, “It was the beginning of a deeply collaborative experience that I hope is equally satisfying for longtime fans of ‘The Simpsons’ and for other South Asian kids who, like me, stopped watching at some point along the way.”

The Simpsons New Apu Voice Actor Breaks Silence on Role

“When my agent called me about a ‘Simpsons’ audition, I knew exactly what role it was for, and the idea actually made my stomach sink,” Maholtra stated about the process while noting that all of the time since Apu’s last speaking appearance could have meant more changes behind the scenes, “But admittedly, part of me was also curious. It had been eight years since Apu had spoken on the show , and it got me thinking: Did the writers’ room look different now? Could they bring him back in a way that acknowledged and apologized for past mistakes?”

“Could I make the character my own, and reclaim him in some way? And could they achieve all of that in an unmistakably ‘Simpsons’ way that didn’t disappoint fans?” Maholtra questioned. The star had not taken to this audition lightly either, “Whether the producers knew it or not, I was prepared to walk away” as he further explained that playing a caricature or stereotypical role was something he wanted to avoid. Even turning down work of a similar nature in the past. But in meeting with the showrunners, Maholtra was relieved to find the process open and collaborative.

“My callback was the first of many times that no one at ‘The Simpsons’ let me down,” the star revealed. “I told casting that I’d only consider an offer if I could meet showrunner Matt Selman and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos , both of whom gladly did so.” Explaining further, the star teases an experience that will hopefully be satisfying for longtime fans, “It was the beginning of a deeply collaborative experience that I hope is equally satisfying for longtime fans of ‘The Simpsons’ and for other South Asian kids who, like me, stopped watching at some point along the way.”

With Azaria vowing to never take on the role again after Apu had been at the center of controversy due to the character’s portrayal of South Asian characteristics, The Simpsons team themselves have been taking their time to reintroduce Apu in a way that would both satisfy fans, and rectify the mistakes of the past. title: CloverWorks' Omnibus Anime Film Grotesqqque Streams 'Yoroshiku★Girl' Segment Early on Netflix for Limited Time
content:
The official website for Atsushi Nishigori 's original anime film Grotesqqque (previously titled Grotesque) announced on Monday that the film's "Yoroshiku★Girl" segment will stream early for a limited time on Netflix in Japan from October 23-November 5, before the film opens on November 6.

The Japan Society hosted the U.S. premiere of the film in collaboration with CloverWorks and Aniplex of America in New York City on October 8. Director Nishigori gave a pre-screening introduction in-person at the event.

The film is an omnibus film of three stories with different worldviews.

• "A(E)liens"

• "Yoroshiku★Girl," (also known as "4649 Girl," pronounced as "Yoroshiku★Shōjo," a pun on the words "Nice to Meet You★Girl" with the literal meaning of the kanji being "Evening Dew Heads to Its Death★Girl." The numbers 4649 can be read in Japanese as "Yoroshiku.")

• "Nocturne: Nuit Grotesque" ("Nocturne: Kono Grotesque na Yoru ni," literally, Nocturne: On This Grotesque Night, romanized in a previous video as "Nocturn: En Cette Nuit Grotesque.")

The film's cast members and characters include :

For the "A(E)liens" story:

• Kana Ichinose as Ellie

• Gen Hoshino as Kento Kurikura

• Akio Ōtsuka as Space Agency Bureau Director

For the "Yoroshiku★Girl" story:

• Sara Minami as Stella

• Ikumi Hasegawa as Unknown (Nanashi)

• Saori Hayami as Hikarin

• Maaya Uchida as Gorgeous Mika

• Chika Anzai as Sword

• Miyu Tomita as Chiffon

• Rumi Ōkubo as Papico

• Rie Kugimiya as Poyomi

For the "Nocturne: Nuit Grotesque" story:

• Nagi Inoue (from Nogizaka46) as Ayame

• Aruno Nakanishi (from Nogizaka46) as Shion

• Miku Ichinose (from Nogizaka46) as Momo

• Nao Tomisato (from Nogizaka46) as Canna

The 35 musical acts contributing to each story in the film are:

"A(E)liens:"

• Mika Ichinose

• VaVa

• Ken Kamikita

• sabio/Fūta Takamura

• SEE

• Surii

• Taku Inoue

• Tsumiki

• Yūshi Nakajima (from Gusokumuzu)

• Nanahira

• Hashimero

"Yoroshiku★Girl"

• ASCA

• Akki

• -otoha-

• Kotoko Satō (from yutori)

• Kanon Shizaki

• Ayato Shinozaki

• JUNNA

• Suisō

• Ryōsuke Tachibana

• Shiina Natsukawa

• Iori Noguchi (from =LOVE)

• Shōta Horie (also known as kemu)

• Myuk

• MIRI

• Rei Yasuda

• Yuyoyuppe

• Runaar

• Reol

"Nocturne: Nuit Grotesque"

• eba

• Nakano+

• Kairi Yagi

Atsushi Nishigori ( The IDOLM@STER , DARLING in the FRANXX ) is directing the film, and is also writing the screenplay and designing the characters.

The band METALVERSE performs the opening theme song "Shoot Shoot Shoot." Haoto performs the ending theme song with lyrics by momosu momosu.

The film comes from JOEN , the company jointly established by Sony media subsidiary Aniplex , its CloverWorks animation studio, Production I.G sister company Wit Studio , and publisher Shueisha . CloverWorks producer Yūichi Fukushima and Wit Studio producer Tetsuya Nakatake are the representative directors of JOEN .

title: Dr. Stone Creator’s New Shonen Jump Series Ends Before Getting a Chance
content:
Dr. Stone remains one of the most iconic and unique Shonen Jump series even several years after the finale. The award-winning manga is written by Riichiro Inagaki and illustrated by Boichi, and began serialization in the Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in 2017. While Boichi is best known for providing the artwork for this fan-favorite sci-fi series, the creator has worked on several manga over the years. Boichi is also famous for providing art and story for several series, including those that have been serialized in Shonen Jump magazines and platforms. His latest work, The Marshal King , sparked quite a lot of hype after its debut thanks to its unique premise.

However, less than two years after the series’ debut, it got axed due to low viewership. The Marshal King featured a post-apocalyptic story with a gorgeous art style that Boichi is known for. Unfortunately, the manga reached its conclusion on October 16th, 2026, with its Chapter 34. The manga went on a hiatus in October last year and returned in September 2026. While the series already had low popularity, the extended hiatus only made things worse. Since the series was bound to get cancelled earlier on, Boichi wrapped up the story in only a month after its return while he continues his work on the spin-off manga for Rokudenashi Blues.

The Marshal King Had a Promising Start, But Couldn’t Live Up to Fans’ Expectations

The Marshal King was by far the most unique series of last year as it focuses on steampunk western themes. The story takes place in a vast, ruined desert wasteland that resembles a futuristic Wild West, following the conflict between chaotic outlaw gangs (desperados) and U.S. Marshals trying to restore law and order. The story centers around Jim Godspeed, a young man and the son of an outlaw, M. Godspeed, who was known as the great villain. For reasons Jim murdered his father and traverses the desert with his body to prove he is the one responsible for the outlaw’s death. The story continues as the truth behind Godspeed’s death and Jim’s real objectives come to light. The series had a perfect balance of mystery and drama, while the art style was just the cherry on top.

Why Was The Marshal King Cancelled?

Shonen Jump series getting cancelled is a common occurrence , even if the publisher doesn’t officially state the reason behind it. The primary reason behind such cancellations is often low popularity and sales, since Shueisha is bound to face certain damage if it continues serializing a manga that won’t catch the reader’s eye. It’s even worse in Weekly Shonen Jump and Shonen Jump +, where the competition is tough and only limited slots are available for creators. If a series isn’t performing well, the publisher will axe it to clear up a slot for other new series that might have a better shot at being successful. The Marshal King had a promising start since Boichi is already a popular character, but the series couldn’t maintain its reader base. Additionally, with the creator working on another project, the hiatus and the sudden cancellation make sense considering his busy schedule.

How do you feel about The Marshal King ‘s cancellation? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

title: Bleach Officially Ends the Anime’s Final Fight After 22 Years With Epic Finale
content:
It’s taken 22 years of waiting until this point, but the newest episode of Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity has officially brought the anime’s final fight to an end with a truly epic finish. Bleach fans have been waiting for over a decade to see the final arc of Tite Kubo’s original manga series to get its own anime adaptation, and the past few years have seen the anime steadily reach this point with the four seasons bringing the final battles to life. Now after an additional month of waiting, the final fight has ended .

When going back to the start of Bleach’ s original TV anime run back in 2004 , it’s been 22 years of Bleach ‘s anime culminating in the release of the franchise’s final two episodes. The first of these two episodes has now hit, and with it brings the fight against Yhwach to its end at last. With lots of events that expand far beyond the scope of the original manga featuring more characters in the middle of the fray, the anime now has the definitive ending to the series overall.

Bleach Finally Ends the Long Fight Against Yhwach in Episode 49

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity Episode 49 picked up right after its cliffhanger before the hiatus last month, and saw Yhwach invading the human world, Soul Society and Hueco Mundo. This was already something that wasn’t seen in Kubo’s original manga version of the finale, but now it’s been expanded a great deal. Not only are even more characters involved as they face off against Yhwach across all three realms, but they help Ichigo to deal the final blow.

The original version of this fight saw Uryu using a special arrowhead given to him by his father to weaken Yhwach enough for Ichigo to deal a decisive blow, and that happens her in the anime as well. But while that’s happening, in Soul Society Captain Kyoraku manages to make it close to Yhwach to touch him and unleash the Right Arm of the Soul King. Meanwhile in Hueco Mundo, Grimmjow and the others piece a blade through Yhwach’s chest. All three Yhwach’s are attacked at the same time, and it leads to his final defeat as originally seen in the manga.

Is the Fight Against Yhwach Really Over?

With how many times Bleach has brought Yhwach back to life after seemingly decisive blows like this, it can be hard to imagine this is truly the end. But with only one episode left, and one final chapter from Kubo’s manga to adapt, this truly is the end of the long fight. The original version of this fight was only about ten pages, and made up of only really 25-30% of the final three chapters of the series. Most of the actual finale is instead spent on exploring the epilogue years after this final bout.

The anime has now made this defeat more decisive than ever before thanks to the way Kubo has been working together with the anime’s production staff to expand on the manga in ways that have elevated the material to new heights. This really is the most conclusive version of the fight, so now all Bleach fans have to do is wait and see how it’s all supposed to end with its final episode next.

How do you feel about the way the Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ended this fight with Yhwach? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Lezhin Ent. to Launch AI Character Chat Service Teaz in Korea
content:
Lezhin Entertainment will launch Teaz, an AI character chat service based on its webtoon intellectual properties (IPs), on October 19 in Korea.

Announced on October 12, Teaz will allow users to interact directly with characters from original series published on Lezhin Comics and Bomtoon . Users can participate in conversations as one of the characters or interact with them from a third-person perspective.

The service uses officially licensed IPs and features relationship-based conversations in which characters' responses and relationships change depending on users' choices. Teaz will also include game-like collection elements, allowing users to collect hidden illustrations and items created by the original webtoon artists.

Teaz will initially launch as a web service, with a mobile app planned for a later date. Additional features, including a text-based role-playing game mode, will be introduced in stages.

Lezhin Entertainment has not yet stated if it will expand the service into English in the future.

Lezhin Entertainment's parent company, KidariStudio, said it will continue expanding its media offerings by combining content IPs with technology.

The launch follows a broader trend of webtoon platforms using AI-powered character chats to expand reader engagement. In July 2026, Naver WEBTOON launched byUs, a story chat service that lets users create narratives with characters from creator-approved webtoon IPs, beginning with Ctrl+Alt+Resign . The company had previously introduced its Character Chat service in South Korea in June 2024, which surpassed 100 million messages by June 2025, before expanding the service to Japan through LINE Manga in February 2026.

The launches by Naver WEBTOON and Lezhin Entertainment reflect growing interest in AI-powered character interactions as a way to extend webtoon IPs beyond their original stories.
